boundary_rationale: Onset: the book opens on two datelines in two counting systems - בִּשְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֗ה (oshb:Ezek.1.1, a regnal/exilic year the book never names an era for) and הַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַחֲמִישִׁ֔ית לְגָל֖וּת הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ יוֹיָכִֽין (oshb:Ezek.1.2, the fifth year of Jehoiachin's exile) - followed at oshb:Ezek.1.3 by the superscription הָיֹ֣ה הָיָ֣ה דְבַר יְ֠הוָה אֶל יְחֶזְקֵ֨אל, an infinitive-absolute-plus-perfect word-event with a THIRD-PERSON addressee ('to Ezekiel', not 'to me'). This verb and addressee shape are why the verse sits in the 49-verse any-form word-event count and not the 48-verse first-person family (sweep: verses containing the word-event phrase in any form, 49; the 48 excludes this one verse by predicate). It is weighed here as a real onset in its own right, not folded into or discounted against the vision that follows. The same verse also carries וַתְּהִ֥י עָלָ֛יו שָׁ֖ם יַד יְהוָֽה, the hand-of-YHWH construct that opens the book's first vision (one of 7 verses carrying the construct). Close: the scene runs unbroken to oshb:Ezek.1.28, מַרְאֵ֖ה דְּמ֣וּת כְּבוֹד יְהוָ֑ה וָֽאֶרְאֶה֙ וָאֶפֹּ֣ל עַל פָּנַ֔י וָאֶשְׁמַ֖ע ק֥וֹל מְדַבֵּֽר, glossed by the WEB as “This was the appearance of the likeness of Yahweh’s glory. When I saw it, I fell on my face, and I heard a voice of one that spoke” (web:Ezek.1.28). No word-event, messenger, recognition or utterance formula interrupts 1:4-1:27 (the transport-verb and 'he said to me' sweeps that mark scene changes elsewhere in the book's visions do not begin until chapter 8), so the throne-theophany carries no formula-marked internal seam; the samekh recorded after 1:28 and the fresh 'he said to me' that opens oshb:Ezek.2.1 together mark the vision/commission seam on the FAR side of this unit; the onset evidence at oshb:Ezek.2.1 is weighed there. The reduced confidence rests on this close, as measured on the witness: 1:28 ends the theophany on a narrative turn, the prophet falling on his face and hearing a voice, with no close-role formula in the verse, so its near face is a discernible close without a counted device, and the samekh recorded after it (single-witness) corroborates that close without deciding it.

boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.2.1 וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלָ֑י בֶּן אָדָם֙ עֲמֹ֣ד עַל רַגְלֶ֔יךָ וַאֲדַבֵּ֖ר אֹתָֽךְ (“He said to me,” and then “Son of man, stand on your feet, and I will speak with you” (web:Ezek.2.1)) opens the commission immediately after the vision's samekh-marked close at oshb:Ezek.1.28 (single-witness). The sending proper follows at 2:3, שׁוֹלֵ֨חַ אֲנִ֤י אֽוֹתְךָ֙ אֶל בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Ezek.2.3) (“I send you to the children of Israel” (web:Ezek.2.3)), continuing into the messenger formula כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.2.4), embedded as reported speech rather than a fresh onset. Pe marks fall after 2:2 and 2:5 (single-witness), disclosed as intra-row sub-paragraph texture, not unit cuts. Close: 2:7, whose last words כִּ֥י מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה (oshb:Ezek.2.7) ('for they are rebellious') end the address on a line that stands in none of the counted close classes, with a pe recorded after that verse. Past it 2:8 renews the address to the same hearer after a verse ending on no close-role formula, so what opens there is a paragraph and not a licensed onset: the near face of this close is a discourse close without formula and its far face carries no signal, and that pairing is what the row's confidence records.

device_notes: Pe marks at 2:2 and 2:5 fall inside the unit and are disclosed as sub-paragraph texture (single-witness); neither coincides with a formula onset, so neither is read as a unit-cutting seam. The phrase בֵּ֥ית מְרִ֖י (oshb:Ezek.2.5) ('rebellious house') recurs at 2:5, inside the same address whose close at 2:7 echoes it. The samekh after oshb:Ezek.1.28 closes the preceding unit's own vision scene and is not this unit's onset evidence. A licensed rival stands inside the row at 2:2/2:3: 2:3 opens וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י (oshb:Ezek.2.3), one of the said-to-me verses that carry an onset inside a vision, and the pe recorded on 2:2 is entered as corroboration for that rival rather than for the row. It is weighed and not taken, because a cut there would leave 2:1-2, two verses that are no complete word-event unit, and because the sending speech at 2:3 addresses the same hearer the commission opened with at 2:1.

boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.2.8 וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֗ם … (WEB “But you, son of man, hear” (web:Ezek.2.8)) turns to the prophet with a ve'attah address, but the addressee does not change, since 2:7 already speaks to him, and 2:7 ends on the rebellion refrain כִּ֥י מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה (oshb:Ezek.2.7), which is no close-role formula; the ve'attah onset is therefore unlicensed, and the pe recorded after oshb:Ezek.2.7 (single-witness) corroborates the break without licensing it. The scroll appears at 2:9, וָאֶרְאֶ֕ה וְהִנֵּה יָ֖ד שְׁלוּחָ֣ה אֵלָ֑י וְהִנֵּה (oshb:Ezek.2.9) (“behold, a hand was stretched out to me” (web:Ezek.2.9)), and its inscription is read at 2:10, אֵלֶ֔יהָ קִנִ֥ים וָהֶ֖גֶה וָהִֽי (oshb:Ezek.2.10) ('lamentations, mourning, and woe'); the samekh recorded after 2:10 stands at the 2:10/3:1 seam and is disclosed as texture inside the row rather than a cut, since the eating that follows continues the same scroll scene: 3:1 reopens with a further 'he said to me,' אֱכוֹל֙ אֶת הַמְּגִלָּ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את (oshb:Ezek.3.1) ('eat this scroll'), intra-row, and the WEB chapter numeral falling at 2:10/3:1 is disclosed only as texture, never as boundary evidence. Close: 3:3, וַתְּהִ֥י בְּפִ֖י כִּדְבַ֥שׁ לְמָתֽוֹק (oshb:Ezek.3.3) ('it was in my mouth as sweet as honey'), with a pe recorded after it, before the address turns from the scroll to the audience's character at 3:4. That close rests on the report of the eating, which carries no close-role formula, while its far face 3:4 opens on a further 'he said to me' inside the vision; with the onset's ve'attah unlicensed and no close-role formula at the close, neither of the row's own near faces carries a licensed signal, which is why the row carries reduced confidence.

boundary_rationale: Onset: 3:4 לֶךְ בֹּא֙ אֶל בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Ezek.3.4) ('go, get you to the house of Israel'), a fresh 'he said to me' turning from the scroll itself to the audience it will be spoken to; 3:7 characterizes them, כִּ֚י כָּל בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל חִזְקֵי מֵ֥צַח וּקְשֵׁי לֵ֖ב הֵֽמָּה (oshb:Ezek.3.7) (“for all the house of Israel are obstinate and hard-hearted” (web:Ezek.3.7)). A pe is recorded after 3:9, כְּשָׁמִ֛יר חָזָ֥ק מִצֹּ֖ר נָתַ֣תִּי מִצְחֶ֑ךָ (“I have made your forehead as a diamond” (web:Ezek.3.9)), closing with a further rebellious-house refrain, כִּ֛י בֵּֽית מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה (oshb:Ezek.3.9) (the third of six). That mark is disclosed but not read as the unit's own close: 3:10 reopens with “Moreover he said to me” (web:Ezek.3.10) on the same audience-description topic, and cutting there would leave 3:10-3:11 (2 verses, no word-event of its own) detached from the speech they continue. Close: 3:11, אִֽם יִשְׁמְע֖וּ וְאִם יֶחְדָּֽלוּ (oshb:Ezek.3.11) (“whether they will hear, or whether they will refuse” (web:Ezek.3.11)), immediately before the return-transport of 3:12 begins a distinct, vision-texture scene.

boundary_rationale: Onset: 3:12 וַתִּשָּׂאֵ֣נִי ר֔וּחַ (oshb:Ezek.3.12) (“Then the Spirit lifted me up” (web:Ezek.3.12)) begins the return-transport away from the plain-vision back to the exiles, distinct in texture from the preceding commissioning speech (no address, no imperative - narrated action). 3:14 carries the hand-of-YHWH construct, וְיַד יְהוָ֥ה עָלַ֖י חָזָֽקָה (oshb:Ezek.3.14) ('the hand of YHWH was strong upon me'), and the same verse carries the transport clause, so, like the onset verse, it stands among the counted transport verses; it is not read as a fresh vision onset here, in contrast to 1:3 and 3:22 - it sits inside a single continuous journey (lifted up → went in bitterness → came to Tel-abib) with no scene change around it, so it is weighed as a licensed rival and held, as the rejected alternative states. Close: 3:15, וָאֵשֵׁ֥ב שָׁ֛ם שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים מַשְׁמִ֥ים בְּתוֹכָֽם (oshb:Ezek.3.15) (“I sat there overwhelmed among them seven days” (web:Ezek.3.15)); no parashah mark is recorded at 3:15 (single-witness), which is not read as counterevidence against the seam. The gap this closes is temporal, not formulaic: 3:16 reopens on “At the end of seven days” (web:Ezek.3.16) with its own strict word-event. What the two seams come to is this: the close near face at 3:15 is the arrival that completes the return movement this row reports, a close in the composition's own voice, and its far face at 3:16 carries the strict word-event; the onset near face at 3:12 carries the transport verb, while its far face 3:11 ends on the sending instruction (oshb:Ezek.3.11) with no close-role formula and no mark (single-witness); and the licensed rival at 3:13/3:14 is weighed and held on the two grounds stated below. That is the strength this row's boundary evidence comes to.

strongest_rejected_alternative: A cut at 3:13/3:14 is the live rival, weighed here face by face and not taken. Its near face, 3:14, carries two candidate drivers at once: the transport clause וְר֥וּחַ נְשָׂאַ֖תְנִי וַתִּקָּחֵ֑נִי (oshb:Ezek.3.14), which places 3:14, like the onset verse 3:12, among the transport verses the book counts (sweep: 33 verses / 46 occurrences), and the hand-of-YHWH construct, which could be read as a fresh vision onset. Its far face, 3:13, is the sound of the creatures' wings and wheels, with no close-role formula and no parashah mark recorded on it (single-witness). Because a transport verb licenses a seam, the rival is not dismissed; it is held on two stated grounds. A row under three verses is held only for a complete word-event unit, and this cut would leave 3:12-13 and 3:14-15 as rows of two verses each, neither of them such a unit. And no scene change accompanies it: the same journey that begins at 3:12 continues without interruption through 3:15, so treating every occurrence of the construct as onset-grade would read a rival this single journey holds as a hard seam.
literature_type_guess: vision return / transport
device_notes: Hand-of-YHWH at 3:14 is one of the book's 7 verses carrying the construct, and it is weighed here as a licensed rival and held rather than taken as a hard seam (contrast the unit-opening uses at 1:3 and 3:22). boundary_rationale: Onset: 3:16 carries the book's first strict word-event formula, וַיְהִ֕י מִקְצֵ֖ה שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֑ים וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.3.16) (“At the end of seven days, Yahweh’s word came to me, saying” (web:Ezek.3.16)), a hard seam, since a strict word-event opens a new oracle and no unit runs across one (3:16 is one of the 39 strict-form verses and one of the 48 in the first-person family). A pe is recorded after this verse (single-witness); this witness's section marks carry no intra-verse position, so no claim is made about where within or after 3:16 the mark stands, ahead of 3:17's watchman charge, צֹפֶ֥ה נְתַתִּ֖יךָ לְבֵ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Ezek.3.17) (“I have made you a watchman to the house of Israel” (web:Ezek.3.17)). A samekh follows 3:19 (single-witness), between the wicked-man case (3:18-19) and the righteous-man case (3:20-21); disclosed as an internal paragraph mark, not a unit cut, since both cases are one paired illustration of the same watchman charge and no fresh onset device stands at 3:20. Close: 3:21, whose last clause turns back on the prophet himself, וְאַתָּ֖ה אֶֽת נַפְשְׁךָ֥ הִצַּֽלְתָּ (oshb:Ezek.3.21), a discourse close the counted close-role forms do not carry; the second samekh stands after that verse (single-witness) and the hand-of-YHWH reopens the scene at 3:22 (oshb:Ezek.3.22) on the far side. The close near face therefore carries a reader-found refrain and no counted formula, and that is the ground of the confidence this row records.

boundary_rationale: Onset: 3:22 וַתְּהִ֥י עָלַ֛י שָׁ֖ם יַד יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Ezek.3.22) (“Yahweh’s hand was there on me” (web:Ezek.3.22)), the hand-of-YHWH construct read here as a genuine vision onset (contrast oshb:Ezek.3.14, where the construct accompanies the spirit carrying the prophet away, a transit rather than a new scene) because it opens a fresh scene: “Arise, go out into the plain” (web:Ezek.3.22). 3:25 announces that עֲבוֹתִ֔ים (oshb:Ezek.3.25) ('ropes') will be put on the prophet; the word recurs at 4:8 in the siege sign-act, across the 3:27/4:1 seam (the same consonants and vowels under a different accent), so the muteness command and the sign-acts share a device, and that continuity is weighed here against the seam even though the unit boundary stands. 3:26 carries the fifth rebellious-house refrain, כִּ֛י בֵּ֥ית מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה. Close: 3:27, הַשֹּׁמֵ֤עַ יִשְׁמָע֙ וְהֶחָדֵ֣ל יֶחְדָּ֔ל כִּ֛י בֵּ֥ית מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה (oshb:Ezek.3.27) (“He who hears, let him hear; and he who refuses, let him refuse; for they are a rebellious house” (web:Ezek.3.27)) - the sixth verse in chapters 2-3 to name the rebellious house (sweep: 12 verses book-wide name it, six of them in chapters 2-3), and the close of the book's opening collection (chapters 1-3); a samekh is recorded after this verse. Across the seam, 4:1 opens with וְאַתָּ֤ה בֶן אָדָם֙ (oshb:Ezek.4.1) ('and you, son of man'), quoted byte for byte as the 3:27 clause is, and turns to the command to take a tile, the sub-onset that starts the sign-acts. The unit therefore stops at 3:27 and does not extend into 4:1; the seam's near side is closed by the refrain and the samekh after 3:27 (single witness), and its far side is opened by that sub-onset.

strongest_rejected_alternative: Placing the seam between the book's first two collections at 3:15/3:16 instead of 3:27/4:1, on the strength of 3:16's own strict word-event and the seven-day close it answers. Weighed on the bytes, the onset side of that seam is strong: 3:16 sets מִקְצֵ֖ה שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֑ים (oshb:Ezek.3.16) (“At the end of seven days” (web:Ezek.3.16)) before its strict word-event, and a pe follows 3:16 itself (single witness), after the word-event verse rather than before it. Its close side is narrative: 3:15 ends the journey to the exiles on seven days of sitting among them, a report rather than a refrain. The rebellious-house refrain runs on both sides of 3:16 (sweep: of the six verses in chapters 2-3 that name the rebellious house, four stand before 3:16 and two after it), so a parent seam there would divide that series, whereas at 3:27/4:1 the series' sixth verse stands on the close side and the sub-onset of 4:1 on the onset side. The alternative is kept as a held question and not argued away, because the ropes of 3:25, taken up at 4:8, tie the muteness command (3:22-27) to the sign-acts (4:1-17) across the later seam.

boundary_rationale: Onset: 4:1 וְאַתָּ֤ה בֶן אָדָם֙ קַח לְךָ֣ לְבֵנָ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.4.1) (“You also, son of man, take a tile” (web:Ezek.4.1)), the 'and you, son of man' sub-onset that stands at the head of the collection this row opens (one of the book's 23 occurrences of that construction), immediately after the parent seam at oshb:Ezek.3.27. The same siege-tile complex continues through the lying sign-acts at 4:4 and the food-rationing at 4:9 without a matching 'son of man' sub-onset at either point (both open with the bare 've'attah' alone), so all three stages read as one commanded symbolic act rather than three. At 4:8, וְהִנֵּ֛ה נָתַ֥תִּי עָלֶ֖יךָ עֲבוֹתִ֑ים (oshb:Ezek.4.8) (“Behold, I put ropes on you” (web:Ezek.4.8)) repeats the consonantal noun of 3:25 across the parent seam, the two tokens differing in accent; the repetition is recorded here as continuity and carries no seam signal of its own. A second address at 4:16, בֶּן אָדָם֙ (oshb:Ezek.4.16), intensifies rather than restarts the act (“behold, I will break the staff of bread” (web:Ezek.4.16)). Close: 4:17, לְמַ֥עַן יַחְסְר֖וּ לֶ֣חֶם וָמָ֑יִם (oshb:Ezek.4.17) (“that they may lack bread and water” (web:Ezek.4.17)), with a pe following it (single-witness), before 5:1 opens a distinct sign-act with its own 'son of man' address.

strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the tile sign-act (4:1-4:3) from the lying and food-rationing sign-acts (4:4-4:17) as two units. How the sign-acts of chs 4-7 divide is an open question, and the 4:3/4:4 seam is its strongest form. The mark on the verse before this cut is weighed as corroboration for the alternative: on the rival's far face the witness records a samekh after oshb:Ezek.4.3 (single-witness), and that verse closes on the sign-act colophon א֥וֹת הִ֖יא לְבֵ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.4.3), “This shall be a sign to the house of Israel” (web:Ezek.4.3), standing verse-final. On the rival's near face the candidate onset oshb:Ezek.4.4 carries no formula whatever: MEASURED over the pointed Hebrew witness, no verse of ch 4 belongs to the counted messenger, utterance, recognition or word-event formula classes, the chapter's only counted device verses being the son-of-man address at 4:1 and 4:16 and the year-word non-datelines at 4:5-4:6. The colophon is not a close-role formula - oshb:Ezek.4.3 is neither an utterance-formula verse (sweep: 81 verses) nor a member of the wide recognition family (sweep: 64 verses) - and the addressee is unchanged across the seam, 2ms imperatives standing to the prophet on either side. A ve'attah inside an open unit begins a sub-unit only when the addressee changes or the verse before it ends on a verse-final close-role formula; neither holds here, and a mark by itself never supplies that close. The rival is therefore paragraph-grade, held on those grounds, and the samekh is disclosed for the alternative it corroborates rather than for this row. The address forms bear this out, 4:3 included, the very verse the mark follows: the titled sub-onset וְאַתָּ֤ה בֶן אָדָם֙ stands at 4:1 and again at 5:1, whereas bare וְאַתָּ֤ה without the title opens three interior stages - 4:3, 4:4 and 4:9 - so the text stages the siege-model, the iron pan, the two lying postures and the rationed food as one commanded act and not as separate commands (oshb:Ezek.4.1).

boundary_rationale: Onset: 5:1 וְאַתָּ֨ה בֶן אָדָ֜ם קַח לְךָ֣ חֶ֣רֶב חַדָּ֗ה (oshb:Ezek.5.1) (“You, son of man, take a sharp sword” (web:Ezek.5.1)), a fresh 'son of man' sub-onset distinct from 4:1's - a new symbolic object (sword/razor/hair) rather than a continuation of the siege-tile act. The messenger formula at 5:5, כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.5.5), opens the act's own interpretation rather than a competing unit (no refrain close intervenes between the hair-sign and its meaning). The oath at 5:11, חַי אָ֗נִי ('as I live'), with the utterance signature נְאֻם֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ (oshb:Ezek.5.11) attached mid-verse, marks an emphatic sub-onset of the verdict paragraph, not a unit boundary. The formula 'I, Yahweh, have spoken' recurs three times, at 5:13 (אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֗ה דִּבַּ֨רְתִּי֙ (oshb:Ezek.5.13)), 5:15 (אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּֽרְתִּי (oshb:Ezek.5.15)) and 5:17 (אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּֽרְתִּי (oshb:Ezek.5.17)); the first two are paragraph-final rather than unit-final because no fresh onset device follows either (5:14 continues “Moreover I will make you a desolation” (web:Ezek.5.14) with no messenger formula or word-event reopening the address). Close: 5:17, with a pe recorded after it, before 6:1 opens with a fresh strict word-event. The verdict continues in two further 'therefore' messenger formulae addressing the same party: 5:7, לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֣י (oshb:Ezek.5.7) (2mp, 'therefore the Lord Yahweh says'), and 5:8, לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י (oshb:Ezek.5.8) (2fs, 'therefore the Lord Yahweh says') — both verdict paragraphs inside the same interpretation, addressing Jerusalem and the people in her as one party, with no refrain standing before either (the samekh after 5:6, 5:7 and 5:9 are disclosed as intra-row texture, not unit-cutting seams). The verdict is bound to the sign-act itself by a byte-identical clause: 5:12 closes with the same words that close 5:2, וְחֶ֖רֶב אָרִ֥יק אַחֲרֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Ezek.5.2; oshb:Ezek.5.12) ('and I will draw a sword after them', sweep: 3 verses book-wide, the third at 12:14).

strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting after 5:13 or after 5:15, the first two 'I Yahweh have spoken' occurrences, to shorten the unit. Rejected because neither is followed by a fresh onset device - the material after each continues the same verdict speech without a messenger formula, word-event or address restarting it - so only 5:17's occurrence is unit-final. The stronger rival, also weighed here, is the 5:4/5:5 seam, where the sign-act command to the prophet ends and the oracle concerning Jerusalem begins, which would set the sign-act 5:1-4 against the interpretation 5:5-17. Its far face carries a PE recorded after oshb:Ezek.5.4 (single witness) and nothing further: that verse ends מִמֶּ֥נּוּ תֵצֵא אֵ֖שׁ אֶל כָּל בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל, and it is neither an utterance-formula verse nor one of the verses of the wide recognition family (sweep: 64 verses), so it does not close on a close-role formula. Its near face is genuinely strong, oshb:Ezek.5.5 carrying the messenger formula כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֔ה verse-initially, “The Lord Yahweh says” (web:Ezek.5.5). But a messenger formula counts as a sub-onset only where the addressee changes or the preceding verse has closed on a verse-final close-role formula, and neither condition holds at this seam: 5:4 addresses the prophet in the 2ms while 5:5 carries no second person at all, the shift to 2mp arriving only at 5:7 and to 2fs at 5:8; and a parashah mark cannot meet the second condition by itself. The row accordingly holds the seam on those stated grounds, and the PE is recorded as corroboration of the rival and not of this unit's onset.

device_notes: 17-verse unit, the whole chapter, over the 7-10 verse target; disclosed as over the target rather than forced into an unsupported internal cut, as at oshb:Ezek.4.1-4.17, since no refrain-plus-fresh-onset pair stands anywhere inside 5:1-5:17 to license a shorter cut. Paseq at 5:1 and 5:7 disclosed count-only, single-witness. Marks after 5:4 (pe), 5:6, 5:7, 5:9 (samekh) and 5:10 (pe) are disclosed as intra-row, single-witness texture. Three of those five marks coincide with a formula onset on the verse following them. The pe after 5:4 stands before the messenger formula at oshb:Ezek.5.5, and the samekh marks after 5:6 and 5:7 stand before the messenger formulae at oshb:Ezek.5.7 and oshb:Ezek.5.8; each of those three verses is one of the 122 verses carrying the long messenger formula, and each carries it verse-initially, 5:7 behind לָכֵ֞ן (oshb:Ezek.5.7) and 5:8 behind לָכֵ֗ן (oshb:Ezek.5.8). The remaining two do not: oshb:Ezek.5.10 opens on לָכֵ֗ן with no messenger formula, and oshb:Ezek.5.11 opens on the oath with the utterance signature attached mid-verse. No one of the five is read as a unit-cutting seam, and the reason is not any absence of coincidence. A messenger formula is a sub-onset when the addressee changes or when the verse before it ENDS on a close-role formula. The second condition fails at all five, since none of 5:4, 5:6, 5:7, 5:9 or 5:10 carries an utterance formula or belongs to the wide recognition family (sweep: 64 verses), and a parashah mark by itself cannot meet it. The first condition does not cut here either: the second-person plural address at 5:7 and the feminine singular at 5:8 turn to Jerusalem and the people within her, whom the verdict treats as a single party, and 5:10 and 5:11 carry no messenger formula at all. Single witness: a pe stands after MT 4:17, the mark this witness sets at the seam where this unit begins.

boundary_rationale: Onset: 6:1 וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.6.1), “Yahweh’s word came to me, saying” (web:Ezek.6.1), a strict word-event, hard seam. 6:2 opens the oracle's direction with שִׂ֥ים פָּנֶ֖יךָ אֶל הָרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Ezek.6.2) (“set your face toward the mountains of Israel” (web:Ezek.6.2)). A 2mp recognition-family close occurs mid-unit at 6:7, וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ם כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.6.7) ('and you shall know that I am Yahweh'); it is disclosed but read as paragraph-final rather than unit-final, since 6:8 continues without a fresh onset device (“Yet I will leave a remnant” (web:Ezek.6.8)). Close: 6:10, the strict recognition formula וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Ezek.6.10) ('and they shall know that I am Yahweh'), with a pe recorded after it (single-witness), immediately before a fresh messenger formula reopens the address at 6:11. That formula does not stand verse-final: לֹ֤א אֶל חִנָּם֙ דִּבַּ֔רְתִּי follows it inside the same verse (oshb:Ezek.6.10), a finite clause with no subordinator, so the close near face carries a formula the verse runs on past - the weaker near-face shape that grounds the confidence this row records, while its far face at 6:11 carries the messenger formula.

boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.11.1 וַתִּשָּׂ֨א אֹתִ֜י ר֗וּחַ וַתָּבֵ֣א אֹ֠תִי אֶל שַׁ֨עַר בֵּית יְהוָ֤ה הַקַּדְמוֹנִי֙ הַפּוֹנֶ֣ה קָדִ֔ימָה וְהִנֵּה֙ בְּפֶ֣תַח הַשַּׁ֔עַר עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֖ה אִ֑ישׁ וָאֶרְאֶ֨ה בְתוֹכָ֜ם אֶת יַאֲזַנְיָ֧ה בֶן עַזֻּ֛ר וְאֶת פְּלַטְיָ֥הוּ בֶן בְּנָיָ֖הוּ שָׂרֵ֖י הָעָֽם — a fresh transport (“the Spirit lifted me up and brought me” (web:Ezek.11.1)) to the east gate, introducing new participants (Jaazaniah son of Azzur, Pelatiah son of Benaiah). The onset itself rests on the transport at 11:1, which carries two guided-motion verbs with the first-person object, 'lifted me up' and 'brought me', while the far face behind it, 10:22, carries no mark and no formula; the witness records no section mark anywhere in chapter 10. Will you make a full end of the remnant of Israel?” (web:Ezek.11.13) — is the prophet's outcry, which the witness's counted close-role formulae do not include; a pe follows this verse as well (single-witness) and corroborates the seam without deciding it. boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.11.14 וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר, the strict word-event formula (one of the book's 39 strict-form onsets), opens an oracle addressed to the exiles rather than to the courtyard men of Ezek.11.1-11.13 — an addressee-class shift inside the vision, from the Jerusalem claimants (oshb:Ezek.11.15, which the WEB renders “This land has been given to us for a possession.” (web:Ezek.11.15)) to “your brothers… the house of Israel” (web:Ezek.11.15) in exile. Close: oshb:Ezek.11.21 וְאֶל לֵ֧ב שִׁקּוּצֵיהֶ֛ם וְתוֹעֲבוֹתֵיהֶ֖ם לִבָּ֣ם הֹלֵ֑ךְ דַּרְכָּם֙ בְּרֹאשָׁ֣ם נָתַ֔תִּי נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה ends with the utterance formula נאם אדני יהוה (one of the book's 81 utterance-close verses). The onset's far face is not: MT 11:13 ends on the prophet's own cry and carries no close-role formula, and the pe recorded after it corroborates the paragraph without supplying one. That one bare far face is the evidence this row's confidence reports. This embedded salvation oracle stands inside the still-open vision (the courtyard scene has not yet returned the prophet — that happens only at 11:22-25) but is bounded by its own onset and close formulae independent of the vision frame, so it is set as its own row rather than folded into 11:1-13 or 11:22-25.

It was not taken because 11:14 is a strict word-event onset (not a bare transition) and the oracle's own addressee — the scattered exiles — differs from the courtyard men addressed in 11:1-13, which is enough of a class shift to justify treating it as its own formula-bounded row even while the wider vision frame stays open around it. A second rival sits inside this row and is weighed here as well: a seam at 11:16/11:17, and behind it a seam at 11:15/11:16. This witness records a samekh after MT 11:15 and another after MT 11:16 (single-witness), and because the witness enters each mark on the verse it stands after, both fall immediately before a verse that carries the long messenger formula כה אמר אדני יהוה — oshb:Ezek.11.16 and oshb:Ezek.11.17, two of that formula's 122 verses. boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.13.17 וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֗ם שִׂ֤ים פָּנֶ֨יךָ֙ אֶל בְּנ֣וֹת עַמְּךָ֔ הַמִּֽתְנַבְּא֖וֹת מִֽלִּבְּהֶ֑ן וְהִנָּבֵ֖א עֲלֵיהֶֽן — “set your face against the daughters of your people” (web:Ezek.13.17) — is one of the book's 9 set-your-face verses and marks an addressee-class shift from the male prophets of 13:1-16, the unit the word-event at oshb:Ezek.13.1 opens, to women “who prophesy out of their own heart” (web:Ezek.13.17). Close: oshb:Ezek.13.23 לָכֵ֗ן שָׁ֚וְא לֹ֣א תֶחֱזֶ֔ינָה וְקֶ֖סֶם לֹא תִקְסַ֣מְנָה ע֑וֹד וְהִצַּלְתִּ֤י אֶת עַמִּי֙ מִיֶּדְכֶ֔ן וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ן כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה ends “Then you will know that I am Yahweh.” (web:Ezek.13.23) in the second-feminine-plural form (וידעתן), a counted form of its own (sweep: 2 verses) that belongs to neither the 3mp-28 nor the 2mp-21 recognition class, though both of its verses are members of the wide recognition family (sweep: 64 verses), whose members are refrain-grade close evidence; a matching 2fp clause also closes the magic-bands sub-paragraph at oshb:Ezek.13.21. Both sides: the onset's near face carries the counted set-your-face command with its address-class shift, and its far face ends on the verse-final utterance signature of oshb:Ezek.13.16, with a pe following that verse (single-witness); the close's near face ends on the counted feminine-plural recognition form at 13:23, still refrain-grade through the wide family and in the two-verse 2fp form rather than the strict or 2mp class, and its far face opens a fresh scene at web:Ezek.14.1 - “Then some of the elders of Israel came to me and sat before me.” (web:Ezek.14.1) - a scene change read off the narrative rather than off any counted formula class. The interior seam at 13:21 is weighed below and opens on no fresh onset. Both seams therefore stand two-faced with no licensed rival against them, and that is what this row's confidence records.

boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.14.1 וַיָּב֤וֹא אֵלַי֙ אֲנָשִׁ֔ים מִזִּקְנֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֵּשְׁב֖וּ לְפָנָֽי — “Then some of the elders of Israel came to me and sat before me.” (web:Ezek.14.1) — is a bare narrative scene-opener with no formula; a pe follows this very verse (single-witness), and the word-event formula proper opens the next verse, oshb:Ezek.14.2 וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר. Close: oshb:Ezek.14.11 לְ֠מַעַן לֹֽא יִתְע֨וּ ע֤וֹד בֵּֽית יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מֵאַֽחֲרַ֔י וְלֹֽא יִטַּמְּא֥וּ ע֖וֹד בְּכָל פִּשְׁעֵיהֶ֑ם וְהָ֥יוּ לִ֣י לְעָ֗ם וַֽאֲנִי֙ אֶהְיֶ֤ה לָהֶם֙ לֵֽאלֹהִ֔ים נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה ends with the utterance formula נאם אדני יהוה; a second pe follows this verse (single-witness), so this witness records a pe on both the first and the last verse of the row, and only the second of them stands at a seam. strongest_rejected_alternative: Opening the row at 14:2, the word-event proper, rather than at 14:1 is the rival that matters, and it is weighed below. On the rival's own side of the seam the evidence is strong: oshb:Ezek.14.2 carries the strict word-event formula, one of that formula's 39 verses. Behind it stands the elders' scene at oshb:Ezek.14.1, which carries no formula of its own. The parashah layer speaks for the RIVAL and not for this row, and it is written up that way: MEASURED in this witness, a pe is recorded on MT 14:1 (single-witness), and the witness keys a break to the verse it follows, so it parts 14:1 from 14:2 — exactly where the rival would cut. Since no mark licenses a seam on its own, the corroboration is disclosed and left unadopted. The row opens at 14:1 all the same, on two stated grounds. First, the elders' scene at 14:1 is the setting the oracle answers, and it comes before the word-event at 14:2, so the row opens at 14:1. Second, a row under three verses is held only for a complete word-event unit, and the one-verse row at 14:1 that the rival's cut would leave behind is no such unit. Holding a licensed rival on stated grounds is what this row's boundary evidence comes to on the rival's side: its far face, 14:1, ends on narrative and stands in no close-role class, so the rival is licensed but not two-faced. The onset near face at 14:1 is a scene change with no device of its own, and that face, together with the licensed rival held at 14:2, is the ground of the confidence this row carries.

strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at oshb:Ezek.14.20, where a pe falls after the fourth triad refrain (single-witness) and immediately before the oracle turns from the hypothetical four scourges to their explicit application to Jerusalem (14:21-23), is the standing rival, and it is weighed here rather than passed over. MT 14:21 opens with a messenger formula: MEASURED on this witness's consonantal skeleton, oshb:Ezek.14.21 begins כי כה אמר אדני יהוה, and that verse is among the 122 verses that carry the long messenger formula. What it opens is nonetheless a paragraph, not a sub-onset, since a messenger sub-onset is granted only where the addressee changes or where the verse just before it ENDS on a close-role formula, and neither condition is met. Nothing marks a new addressee at 14:21 — MEASURED, the son-of-man address falls at MT 14:3 and MT 14:13 and at no other verse of this chapter, chapter 14 carries no set-your-face verse at all, and 14:21 is not opened by 'and you, son of man' — so what turns there is the subject, from a hypothetical land to Jerusalem, and not the person addressed. As for the second condition, the utterance formula in MT 14:20 does NOT reach the verse end: MEASURED, נאם אדני יהוה sits at characters 29 through 41 of an 81-character skeleton, the first character counted as 1 and both ends included, and from there the oath's own content runs to the etnachta, with אם בן אם בת יצילו המה בצדקתם יצילו נפשם standing between that signature and the sof pasuq, its second clause independent after the major disjunctive. So the pe on MT 14:20 is entered as support for the rival it favours and for no more than that: this witness records the break after MT 14:20, a mark cannot supply the verse-final close-role formula that the second condition asks for, and paragraph evidence informs while every licensed driver outranks it. The row carries on to its own verse-final utterance close at oshb:Ezek.14.23.

Paseq at 14:21 is count-only, single-witness. oshb:Ezek.15.1 is cited above only as forward-side onset evidence for the seam; it is not a row here. boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 15:1 opens with the strict word-event formula, וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.15.1), immediately followed by the address בֶּן אָדָ֕ם (oshb:Ezek.15.2) at 15:2, which puts the riddle about the useless vine-wood in the standard oracle-onset frame. Close side: the row's final verse, MT 15:8, ends the applied sentence against Jerusalem's inhabitants and carries the utterance-of-the-Lord-YHWH signature at its own end, matched by a pe mark recorded on 15:8 in the single-witness paragraph layer. A samekh mark sits earlier, on 15:5 (sweep: 8 verses), where the riddle's own question -- whether the vine-wood, even charred, is fit for any use -- reaches its rhetorical dead end before the messenger formula כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.15.6) opens the application at 15:6. That mid-chapter mark is weighed and not adopted as the row seam: the application (15:6-8) answers the riddle (15:1-5) rather than opening an independent formula-bounded unit of its own, and a three-verse application row would not itself carry a fresh word-event onset. The row is therefore kept as the whole chapter, with the internal mark disclosed rather than acted on. The pe marks after MT 14:23 and on 15:8 confirm both outer seams but settle nothing inside the chapter, where a samekh on 15:5 and the messenger formula at 15:6 mark a rival cut the row declines by argument against that mark, and that is the ground of the confidence this row records.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: the word-event formula וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.16.1) at 16:1, the address בֶּן אָדָ֕ם (oshb:Ezek.16.2) at 16:2, and the messenger formula naming the addressee, כֹּה אָמַ֨ר אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ לִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם (oshb:Ezek.16.3) at 16:3, together open the foundling allegory and fix Jerusalem as the figure's referent from the first clause; the pe recorded at MT 15:8 (single witness) closes the unit before it, corroborating this row's onset from the far side of the seam. Close side: MT 16:14 is this row's last verse, and its own final words are the utterance formula נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.16.14), closing the first movement (the abandoned infant clothed, fed and enthroned) before the narrative turns to her unfaithfulness at 16:15. No parashah mark falls between 16:1 and 16:14 (sweep: 14 verses), so the utterance-formula close is the only mark-independent boundary evidence available for this stretch, and it is taken as such. MT 16:13 (oshb:Ezek.16.13) carries a doubled Ketiv/Qere note inside this span: the running text reads the ketiv forms ששי and אכלתי in place of the pointed readings; the Qere layer gives (Qere for both) שֵׁ֤שׁ (fine linen) and אָכָ֑לְתְּ (you ate) respectively. Neither Qere is used to argue this boundary; both are disclosed because the span covers them.

Its far face, MT 16:43, ends the preceding speech, but its utterance formula נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.16.43) stands mid-verse, with the lewdness clause running past it to the sof pasuq, so no verse-final close-role formula sits behind this onset either. So the close stands two-faced while the onset's near face carries no licensed signal, and that unlicensed near face, at a seam the plan names on content, is the ground of this row's confidence. Two interior seams are weighed and held, both paragraph-grade: at 16:50/16:51 the comparison turns to Samaria after the samekh recorded on 16:50 (single-witness) and meets a verse with no onset device, and at 16:52/16:53 the restoration turn opens with no device of its own. boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 16:59 opens with the messenger formula כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.16.59) ('for thus says the Lord YHWH'), turning from the sisters comparison to YHWH's own covenant memory; the running text reads the ketiv ועשית in place of the pointed form here (oshb:Ezek.16.59). Close side: the row runs to the chapter's own end, MT 16:63, the whole verse לְמַ֤עַן תִּזְכְּרִי֙ וָבֹ֔שְׁתְּ וְלֹ֨א יִֽהְיֶה לָּ֥ךְ עוֹד֙ פִּתְח֣וֹן פֶּ֔ה מִפְּנֵ֖י כְּלִמָּתֵ֑ךְ בְּכַפְּרִי לָךְ֙ לְכָל אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֔ית נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.16.63), whose final words are the utterance formula, matched by a samekh recorded on this same verse -- the strongest close available in the chapter, mark, refrain and chapter-end all coinciding. Inside the row, MT 16:62 closes with the second-person recognition formula, the whole verse וַהֲקִימוֹתִ֥י אֲנִ֛י אֶת בְּרִיתִ֖י אִתָּ֑ךְ וְיָדַ֖עַתְּ כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.16.62) ('and you shall know that I am YHWH'), a genuine refrain close that is nonetheless not treated as the row's own end, since 16:63 both continues the same covenant sentence grammatically and carries the stronger, mark-corroborated close.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 17:1 opens (oshb:Ezek.17.1) with the strict word-event formula וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר, and 17:2 names the genre directly, בֶּן אָדָ֕ם ח֥וּד חִידָ֖ה וּמְשֹׁ֣ל מָשָׁ֑ל אֶל בֵּ֖ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.17.2) (rendered “Son of man, tell a riddle, and speak a parable to the house of Israel”, web:Ezek.17.2), before the messenger formula כֹּה אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה (oshb:Ezek.17.3) opens the eagle-and-vine figure itself. Close side: this row runs through 17:10, whose concluding clause תִּיבַ֣שׁ יָבֹ֔שׁ (oshb:Ezek.17.10) ('it will surely wither') answers the riddle's own rhetorical question, matched by a pe recorded on this same verse in the single-witness paragraph layer -- the riddle's content is complete and the mark coincides with it, so the row is closed here before the interpretation opens with its own word-event formula at 17:11. The onset is two-faced, 16:63 ending on the utterance formula verse-finally with a samekh after it against the word-event formula at 17:1. The close is not: its near face, 17:10, ends on the riddle's answer with no close-role formula, a content close the book-wide formula counts do not list, and the pe is corroboration that licenses nothing. That near face, against the word-event formula on the far face at 17:11, is what keeps the row's confidence reduced.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 18:1 opens on the strict word-event formula וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.18.1); 18:2 quotes the popular proverb the oracle will refute, אָבוֹת֙ יֹ֣אכְלוּ בֹ֔סֶר וְשִׁנֵּ֥י הַבָּנִ֖ים תִּקְהֶֽינָה (oshb:Ezek.18.2) (“The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children’s teeth are set on edge”, web:Ezek.18.2). Close side: the span closes at 18:4, whose final clause הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַחֹטֵ֖את הִ֥יא תָמֽוּת (oshb:Ezek.18.4) ('the soul who sins shall die') states the disputation's thesis, and a samekh stands on this same verse (single-witness). An oath formula with the utterance signature stands at the head of 18:3, in that verse's first five words ('as I live, declares the Lord YHWH'), weighed as texture inside the refutation rather than a row-final close, since the clause on the proverb's future use runs on after it to the end of the same verse. The close at 18:4/18:5 is a case turn inside one word-event unit: 18:4 ends on the disputation's thesis and carries a samekh, 18:5 opens the righteous-man case with no formula of its own, and the samekh corroborates that turn without deciding it. A close seam of that shape holds a row at reduced confidence, and this row is held there. The onset seam, by contrast, is two-faced and top grade: 17:24 ends on the I-YHWH-have-spoken formula, verse-final, with a pe recorded after it (single-witness), against 18:1's strict word-event formula.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 18:5 opens with no formula device, the whole verse וְאִ֖ישׁ כִּי יִהְיֶ֣ה צַדִּ֑יק וְעָשָׂ֥ה מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּצְדָקָֽה (oshb:Ezek.18.5) ('if a man is righteous and does what is just and right'), a default case-law onset following the thesis stated at 18:4; the samekh recorded there (single-witness), closing the unit before it, corroborates this row's onset from the far side of the seam. The two seams differ in shape, and the onset seam is the weaker: measured on the witness, its near face carries no device at all and its far face ends on the thesis without a close formula, which is what holds the row at reduced confidence; the close seam’s near face at least ends on the utterance formula, though nothing answers it at 18:10.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 18:10 opens with no formula device, the whole verse וְהוֹלִ֥יד בֵּן פָּרִ֖יץ שֹׁפֵ֣ךְ דָּ֑ם וְעָ֣שָׂה אָ֔ח מֵאַחַ֖ד מֵאֵֽלֶּה (oshb:Ezek.18.10) ('and he fathers a violent son who sheds blood'), continuing the case-law series by default. The righteous grandson's case (18:14) and the summary restatement (18:19-20) follow without any fresh formula onset of their own, since 18:18 explicitly recalls the father's own guilt from 18:10-13 before drawing the general rule -- one continuous legal argument across three generations, not three independently onset units. boundary_rationale: Onset: 18:21 opens the case of the wicked man who turns, וְהָרָשָׁ֗ע כִּ֤י יָשׁוּב֙ (oshb:Ezek.18.21) (“But if the wicked turns from all his sins” (web:Ezek.18.21)), with no onset-class device of its own; its far face 18:20 closes the preceding case on the principle that a person's own righteousness or wickedness rests on that person, and ends on no close-role formula, the samekh after it (single-witness) corroborating the break only. Close: 18:32 carries the utterance formula נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה (oshb:Ezek.18.32) mid-verse, and the independent imperative וְהָשִׁ֖יבוּ וִֽחְיֽוּ (oshb:Ezek.18.32) follows it, “Therefore turn yourselves, and live!” (web:Ezek.18.32), so the formula does not stand at the verse's end; a pe follows the verse, and the far face 19:1 opens on the command to take up a lament, וְאַתָּה֙ שָׂ֣א קִינָ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.19.1). Between these seams the span makes one appeal: the wicked man who turns (18:21-23), the righteous man who turns away (18:24), the people's objection, the two cases restated and the objection repeated (18:25-29), and the closing appeal (18:30-32). The utterance formula standing mid-verse in 18:23 with a samekh after it, the samekh after 18:26, and the therefore-turn at 18:30 mark paragraphs inside that one appeal, and none of them carries a licensed onset. Neither of the row's own near faces carries a licensed signal, since the onset opens with no formula and the close's formula stands mid-verse, and only the far face of the close, 19:1, is licensed; the row is held at reduced confidence on those faces.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: the pe recorded at MT 18:32 (single witness) closes the preceding unit before it, corroborating this row's onset from the far side of the seam; MT 19:1 itself opens with the distinct qinah-command onset וְאַתָּה֙ שָׂ֣א קִינָ֔ה אֶל נְשִׂיאֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.19.1) (“Moreover, take up a lamentation for the princes of Israel”, web:Ezek.19.1) -- not a word-event formula and not a son-of-man address, but the genre-naming command proper to a lament. Close side: the row runs to the chapter's own colophon, MT 19:14, the whole verse וַתֵּצֵ֨א אֵ֜שׁ מִמַּטֵּ֤ה בַדֶּ֨יהָ֙ פִּרְיָ֣הּ אָכָ֔לָה וְלֹא הָ֥יָה בָ֛הּ מַטֵּה עֹ֖ז שֵׁ֣בֶט לִמְשׁ֑וֹל קִ֥ינָה הִ֖יא וַתְּהִ֥י לְקִינָֽה (oshb:Ezek.19.14), whose last clause names its own genre a second time (“This is a lamentation, and shall be for a lamentation”, web:Ezek.19.14), matched by a pe recorded on this same verse. A pe also falls mid-chapter, on 19:9, at the close of the lion-cubs figure (אֲרָי֖וֹת, oshb:Ezek.19.2) -- לְמַ֗עַן לֹא יִשָּׁמַ֥ע קוֹל֛וֹ ע֖וֹד אֶל הָרֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.19.9) (“so that his voice should no more be heard on the mountains of Israel”, web:Ezek.19.9) -- immediately before the second figure opens at 19:10, אִמְּךָ֥ כַגֶּ֛פֶן בְּדָמְךָ֖ עַל מַ֣יִם שְׁתוּלָ֑ה (oshb:Ezek.19.10) (“Your mother was like a vine in your blood, planted by the waters”, web:Ezek.19.10). That internal mark is disclosed and weighed, not adopted as a row seam: the lament noun that opens the chapter at 19:1 returns in the colophon at 19:14, which names the composition a lamentation, so the span is kept as one row rather than split at its own internal parashah break.

In the WEB, “Yahweh’s word came to me, saying,” (web:Ezek.25.1). 25:2 supplies the addressee, "בֶּן אָדָ֕ם שִׂ֥ים פָּנֶ֖יךָ אֶל בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֑וֹן וְהִנָּבֵ֖א עֲלֵיהֶֽם" (oshb:Ezek.25.2) — the set-your-face command “toward the children of Ammon” (web:Ezek.25.2, WEB) is the first of the book's set-your-face verses (sweep: 9 verses) to name a foreign nation, and the class shift that opens the oracles-against-the-nations collection; Ammon itself is not a new addressee here, since the sword oracle at MT 21:33 (= WEB 21:28) already concerns the children of Ammon. Close (weighed from both sides): 25:7 ends "לָכֵ֡ן הִנְנִי֩ נָטִ֨יתִי אֶת יָדִ֜י עָלֶ֗יךָ וּנְתַתִּ֤יךָֽ לבג לַגּוֹיִ֔ם וְהִכְרַתִּ֨יךָ֙ מִן הָ֣עַמִּ֔ים וְהַאֲבַדְתִּ֖יךָ מִן הָאֲרָצ֑וֹת אַשְׁמִ֣ידְךָ֔ וְיָדַעְתָּ֖ כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה" (oshb:Ezek.25.7; לבג there is the verse’s ketiv, Qere לְבַז֙), closing on the 2ms recognition variant "and you shall know that I am YHWH" with a SAMEKH immediately after. An earlier internal close sits at 25:5, "וְנָתַתִּ֤י אֶת רַבָּה֙ לִנְוֵ֣ה גְמַלִּ֔ים וְאֶת בְּנֵ֥י עַמּ֖וֹן לְמִרְבַּץ צֹ֑אן וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ם כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה" (oshb:Ezek.25.5), which also ends on a 2mp recognition-family clause (the wider 2mp recognition family, sweep: 21 verses, includes 25:5, not the 2s list, sweep: 5 verses (gender unresolved on the skeleton)) and carries its own SAMEKH. Because a refrain closes the unit before it, both 25:5 and 25:7 are treated as closes; they are kept in one row because 25:6 reopens with a coordinating messenger formula ("כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה", oshb:Ezek.25.6) against the same addressee (Ammon) rather than a fresh nation, so no addressee-class shift separates 25:5 from 25:7. The 25:5/25:6 seam is therefore a licensed rival carrying a signal on both of its faces - the coordinating messenger formula on its near face at 25:6, and on its far face a verse-final recognition-family clause at 25:5 with a samekh after it (single witness) - and it is held on the stated ground that the addressee does not change; that held rival is what places this row's confidence at the middle of the scale. Ahead of this row, 25:8 opens a fresh messenger formula with an addressee change to Moab, the row's forward hard seam.

boundary_rationale: Onset: 25:12 opens with the messenger formula and a fresh addressee, "כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה יַ֣עַן עֲשׂ֥וֹת אֱד֛וֹם בִּנְקֹ֥ם נָקָ֖ם לְבֵ֣ית יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיֶּאְשְׁמ֥וּ אָשׁ֖וֹם וְנִקְּמ֥וּ בָהֶֽם" (oshb:Ezek.25.12) — Edom — again a messenger-formula addressee-change cut. In the WEB, “Because Edom has dealt against the house of Judah by taking vengeance, and has greatly offended, and taken revenge on them,” (web:Ezek.25.12). Close (both sides): 25:14 ends "וְנָתַתִּ֨י אֶת נִקְמָתִ֜י בֶּאֱד֗וֹם בְּיַד֙ עַמִּ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְעָשׂ֣וּ בֶאֱד֔וֹם כְּאַפִּ֖י וְכַחֲמָתִ֑י וְיָֽדְעוּ֙ אֶת נִקְמָתִ֔י נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה" (oshb:Ezek.25.14), carrying a PE immediately after (single-witness). The close itself is a disclosed deviation from the strict recognition formula: the verb clause reads "and they shall know MY VENGEANCE" (an object noun, not "that I am YHWH"), stacked with the utterance-of-the-Lord-YHWH signature, "נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה" (oshb:Ezek.25.14); it belongs to the utterance list (sweep: 81 verses), not the strict recognition list (sweep: 28 verses) or either 2ms/2mp recognition family. Behind this row, 25:11 closed Moab on the strict 3mp recognition + SAMEKH (single-witness); ahead, 25:15 opens a fresh messenger formula with the addressee change to the Philistines. Both faces of both seams therefore carry signals the witness counts; what holds this row's confidence lower is the shape of the division itself, which the plan leaves open for these oracles — four short rows, two, or one seventeen-verse row — with this row standing as one of the four.

boundary_rationale: Onset: 26:1 opens "וַיְהִ֛י בְּעַשְׁתֵּֽי עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה שָׁנָ֖ה בְּאֶחָ֣ד לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ הָיָ֥ה דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר" (oshb:Ezek.26.1) — a year-and-day dateline whose month is not named (“In the eleventh year, in the first of the month”, web:Ezek.26.1, WEB) together with the PERFECT-form word-event, "הָיָ֥ה דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר" (oshb:Ezek.26.1), the 7-verse hayah family the dated oracles use after their dateline, a HARD seam and the strongest onset class in the book. In the WEB, “In the eleventh year, in the first of the month, Yahweh’s word came to me, saying,” (web:Ezek.26.1). 26:2 supplies the accusation, "בֶּן אָדָ֗ם יַ֠עַן אֲשֶׁר אָ֨מְרָה צֹּ֤ר עַל יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ הֶאָ֔ח נִשְׁבְּרָ֛ה דַּלְת֥וֹת הָעַמִּ֖ים נָסֵ֣בָּה אֵלָ֑י אִמָּלְאָ֖ה הָחֳרָֽבָה" (oshb:Ezek.26.2), quoting Tyre's own "Aha!" against Jerusalem. Close (both sides): 26:6 ends "וּבְנוֹתֶ֨יהָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה בַּחֶ֖רֶב תֵּהָרַ֑גְנָה וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה" (oshb:Ezek.26.6), the strict 3mp recognition formula, with a PE immediately after (single-witness). Ahead, 26:7 reopens with a fresh messenger formula ("כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה הִנְנִ֧י מֵבִ֣יא אֶל צֹ֗ר…", oshb:Ezek.26.7) introducing Nebuchadnezzar's siege — a new speech unit against the same addressee, not an addressee change, which is why it is held as its own row rather than folded in here: the refrain at 26:6 closes THIS unit. The onset's far face is the mid-verse recognition at 25:17 rather than a verse-final close, and the plan flags this chapter among those where onset and close collide, holding four messenger units, one row per unit, as its default, so this row's confidence stays below what its close seam alone would carry.

boundary_rationale: Onset: 26:7 reopens with the messenger formula, "כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה הִנְנִ֧י מֵבִ֣יא אֶל צֹ֗ר נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֧ר מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶ֛ל מִצָּפ֖וֹן מֶ֣לֶךְ מְלָכִ֑ים בְּס֛וּס וּבְרֶ֥כֶב וּבְפָרָשִׁ֖ים וְקָהָ֥ל וְעַם רָֽב" (oshb:Ezek.26.7), introducing Nebuchadnezzar's siege by name — a fresh speech unit following the 26:6 close. In the WEB, “For the Lord Yahweh says: ‘Behold, I will bring on Tyre Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, king of kings, from the north, with horses, with chariots, with horsemen, and an army with many people.” (web:Ezek.26.7). Close (both sides): 26:14 ends "וּנְתַתִּ֞יךְ לִצְחִ֣יחַ סֶ֗לַע מִשְׁטַ֤ח חֲרָמִים֙ תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה לֹ֥א תִבָּנֶ֖ה ע֑וֹד כִּ֣י אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ דִּבַּ֔רְתִּי נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה" (oshb:Ezek.26.14), stacking TWO closes in one verse — "for I YHWH have spoken" (the 14-verse emphatic-close family) and the utterance-of-the-Lord-YHWH signature (the 81-verse family) — with a samekh immediately after (single-witness). How chapter 26 divides - one row for each of its four messenger units, or fewer - is an open question here, and that question, not these faces, is what holds this row at reduced confidence, on the same reading the preceding unit of the chapter carries. Behind, 26:6 closed the first unit on the recognition formula with a pe recorded on that verse (single-witness); ahead, 26:15 reopens with a further fresh messenger formula shifting from direct 2fs address of Tyre's destruction to the scene of the sea-princes' reaction.

Close: a pe mark follows Ezek.33.22 (single-witness), and the verse completes the narrative beat before Ezek.33.23 opens a fresh, formally distinct word-event oracle. The onset's near face is licensed -- the dateline itself -- while the far face behind it carries that mark and no formula. The close's near face, 33:22, carries no close-role signal: its hand-of-YHWH idiom is narrative notice, and the verse ends on the mouth-opening clause with no formula, while its far face is 33:23's fresh word-event formula. That close near face is the ground of this row's reduced confidence.

Five K/Q notes fall inside the span, two at 36:13, two at 36:14 and one at 36:15, their ketiv and qere forms listed with the references (single-witness apparatus); none is argued for a boundary. Paseq is recorded once within 36:5 and once within 36:6 (count-only, single-witness); the position of either stroke within its verse is not stated. An editors’ note on the accents stands at 36:7 (single-witness apparatus), disclosed and not argued. The row’s burden is the restoration of the mountains, their tilling, sowing and resettlement, and the end of the nations’ taunt against the land, which places it among the restoration promises rather than the oracles against foreign nations, though it shares the frame of 35:1 with the Seir oracle. Length disclosed as a fact: 15 verses, against the target of 7-10 verses per row.

boundary_rationale: Onset: a samekh follows MT 36:15 (single-witness), the paragraph mark behind this unit's onset. A fresh strict-form word-event formula crosses a hard seam at Ezek.36.16 וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.36.16), the fifth such hard seam since Ezek.33.1 (33.1, 33.23, 34.1, 35.1, 36.16) and not the last — 37.15 and 38.1 follow. 'Son of man' at Ezek.36.17 בֶּן אָדָ֗ם בֵּ֤ית יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יֹשְׁבִ֣ים עַל אַדְמָתָ֔ם וַיְטַמְּא֣וּ אוֹתָ֔הּ בְּדַרְכָּ֖ם וּבַעֲלִֽילוֹתָ֑ם כְּטֻמְאַת֙ הַנִּדָּ֔ה הָיְתָ֥ה דַרְכָּ֖ם לְפָנָֽי (oshb:Ezek.36.17) opens a retrospective on Israel's own defilement of the land and the resulting exile — a distinct tense and topic from the 'mountains of Israel' address just closed. Inside the span a samekh follows MT 36:21 (single-witness); the unit does not cut there because the messenger-formula pivot at Ezek.36.22 לָכֵ֞ן אֱמֹ֣ר לְבֵֽית יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה לֹ֧א לְמַעַנְכֶ֛ם אֲנִ֥י עֹשֶׂ֖ה בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּ֤י אִם לְשֵׁם קָדְשִׁי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חִלַּלְתֶּ֔ם בַּגּוֹיִ֖ם אֲשֶׁר בָּ֥אתֶם שָֽׁם (oshb:Ezek.36.22) (“I don’t do this for your sake” (web:Ezek.36.22)) opens with a 'therefore' consequence-clause: it draws out the result of the profanation narrated in the third person at Ezek.36.20 וַיָּב֗וֹא אֶל הַגּוֹיִם֙ אֲשֶׁר בָּ֣אוּ שָׁ֔ם וַֽיְחַלְּל֖וּ אֶת שֵׁ֣ם קָדְשִׁ֑י בֶּאֱמֹ֤ר לָהֶם֙ עַם יְהוָ֣ה אֵ֔לֶּה וּמֵאַרְצ֖וֹ יָצָֽאוּ (oshb:Ezek.36.20) and Ezek.36.21 וָאֶחְמֹ֖ל עַל שֵׁ֣ם קָדְשִׁ֑י אֲשֶׁ֤ר חִלְּל֨וּהוּ֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בַּגּוֹיִ֖ם אֲשֶׁר בָּ֥אוּ שָֽׁמָּה (oshb:Ezek.36.21), where 'my holy name' is twice named as the thing profaned, and the same holy-name argument runs from there through 36.22 to the utterance close at 36.23. The turn from third-person narration to second-person address at 36.22 is disclosed here as a sub-onset within that one argument, not as an addressee change that would cut the unit. Close: the utterance formula at Ezek.36.23 וְקִדַּשְׁתִּ֞י אֶת שְׁמִ֣י הַגָּד֗וֹל הַֽמְחֻלָּל֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר חִלַּלְתֶּ֖ם בְּתוֹכָ֑ם וְיָדְע֨וּ הַגּוֹיִ֜ם כִּי אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֗ה נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה בְּהִקָּדְשִׁ֥י בָכֶ֖ם לְעֵינֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Ezek.36.23), whose own bytes carry, immediately before the utterance formula, a recognition clause addressed to the nations, one of the 64 such verses book-wide and refrain-grade in class. Both that clause and the utterance signature stand mid-verse: the verse runs on after נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה with a dependent temporal infinitive, and no mark is recorded on it (single-witness). Its far face, 36.24, opens on no particle of any tracked class, belongs to no device class and carries no mark (single-witness; oshb:Ezek.36.24); the seam therefore rests on its near face alone. On a strict verse-final test that close is mid-verse; read with its dependent completion, a recognition clause and an utterance signature followed by nothing but a temporal infinitive, it stands as an ordinary licensed close, and that disclosed reading of the near face is what this row's boundary evidence records.

boundary_rationale: Onset: 36:24 opens on a plain weqatal, וְלָקַחְתִּ֤י אֶתְכֶם֙ מִן הַגּוֹיִ֔ם וְקִבַּצְתִּ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם מִכָּל הָאֲרָצ֑וֹת וְהֵבֵאתִ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם אֶל אַדְמַתְכֶֽם (oshb:Ezek.36.24) - no particle and no counted device stands at its head, and the English 'For' is the translation's connective rather than anything this witness carries - continuing the shared Ezek.36.16 word-event frame (disclosed, verse-anchored) and opening the gather-and-return material. Sprinkling and cleansing follow at Ezek.36.25, then MT 36.26 reads וְנָתַתִּ֤י לָכֶם֙ לֵ֣ב חָדָ֔שׁ וְר֥וּחַ חֲדָשָׁ֖ה אֶתֵּ֣ן בְּקִרְבְּכֶ֑ם וַהֲסִ֨רֹתִ֜י אֶת לֵ֤ב הָאֶ֨בֶן֙ מִבְּשַׂרְכֶ֔ם וְנָתַתִּ֥י לָכֶ֖ם לֵ֥ב בָּשָֽׂר (oshb:Ezek.36.26), reading 'a new heart', spliced directly from this witness, in explicit contrast with MT 11.19, which in this same witness reads וְנָתַתִּ֤י לָהֶם֙ לֵ֣ב אֶחָ֔ד וְר֥וּחַ חֲדָשָׁ֖ה אֶתֵּ֣ן בְּקִרְבְּכֶ֑ם וַהֲסִ֨רֹתִ֜י לֵ֤ב הָאֶ֨בֶן֙ מִבְּשָׂרָ֔ם וְנָתַתִּ֥י לָהֶ֖ם לֵ֥ב בָּשָֽׂר (oshb:Ezek.11.19), reading “one heart” (web:Ezek.11.19) (with 'a new spirit' as the item that is new there): Ezek.11.19 is not a 'new heart' verse in WLC/OSHB, though the wider manuscript and versional tradition often reads it that way; this observation is scoped to this single witness and claims nothing about that wider tradition. The covenant formula “You will be my people, and I will be your God.” (web:Ezek.36.28) follows at Ezek.36.28. Close: the utterance formula at Ezek.36.32 לֹ֧א לְמַעַנְכֶ֣ם אֲנִֽי עֹשֶׂ֗ה נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה יִוָּדַ֖ע לָכֶ֑ם בּ֧וֹשׁוּ וְהִכָּלְמ֛וּ מִדַּרְכֵיכֶ֖ם בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.36.32) (“I don't do this for your sake” and “Let it be known to you. Be ashamed”, both web:Ezek.36.32); the close at MT 36:32 carries a samekh (single-witness). That utterance stands mid-verse, with independent imperatives running on after it to the verse's end, so the close's near face is a weak one; with the onset's near face at 36:24 carrying no device at all, those two near faces are what this row's confidence records.

boundary_rationale: Onset: the verse opens on the hand-of-YHWH idiom immediately followed by a transport verb, oshb:Ezek.37.1 הָיְתָ֣ה עָלַי֮ יַד יְהוָה֒ וַיּוֹצִאֵ֤נִי בְר֨וּחַ֙ יְהוָ֔ה וַיְנִיחֵ֖נִי בְּת֣וֹךְ הַבִּקְעָ֑ה וְהִ֖יא מְלֵאָ֥ה עֲצָמֽוֹת -- the same onset shape that opens the book's other three long prose visions, and this occurrence is one of only 7 hand-of-YHWH verses in the book. The unit is held as one scene, with the live rival inside it weighed below: the prophet is set down among the bones (37.1-2), questioned and commanded to prophesy twice -- once to the bones, once to the breath/spirit (37.4-6, 37.9), watches the two-stage reanimation (37.7-8, 37.10), and receives the scene's own interpretation as a word to 'son of man' (oshb:Ezek.37.11 וַיֹּאמֶר֮ אֵלַי֒ בֶּן אָדָ֕ם הָעֲצָמ֣וֹת הָאֵ֔לֶּה כָּל בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הֵ֑מָּה הִנֵּ֣ה אֹמְרִ֗ים יָבְשׁ֧וּ עַצְמוֹתֵ֛ינוּ וְאָבְדָ֥ה תִקְוָתֵ֖נוּ נִגְזַ֥רְנוּ לָֽנוּ). Close: oshb:Ezek.37.14 stacks three refrain-grade closes in one verse -- the second-person plural recognition variant (the knowing clause addressed to the hearers in the plural, part of a 21-verse 2mp family sweep), the emphatic 'I YHWH have spoken' close (one of 14 book-wide), and the short utterance signature without the divine-name pair (one of only 4 such short forms in the book) -- וְנָתַתִּ֨י רוּחִ֤י בָכֶם֙ וִחְיִיתֶ֔ם וְהִנַּחְתִּ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם עַל אַדְמַתְכֶ֑ם וִידַעְתֶּ֞ם כִּי אֲנִ֧י יְהוָ֛ה דִּבַּ֥רְתִּי וְעָשִׂ֖יתִי נְאֻם יְהוָֽה, and a pe mark is recorded immediately after this verse (single-witness, informing not deciding). Both sides of the following seam were weighed: oshb:Ezek.37.15 opens with the strict word-event formula וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר, one of 39 verses carrying that strict form, so the close at 37.14 and the fresh onset at 37.15 corroborate each other from both directions. Both faces of that close are top grade; measured on the witness, the row stands one step below the top grade because a licensed rival lies inside the span, at the 37.10/37.11 seam.

boundary_rationale: Onset: the strict word-event formula reopens at oshb:Ezek.37.15 וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר, following the pe mark recorded after oshb:Ezek.37.14 (behind this row, single-witness, closing the unit before it) and followed at 37.16 by the commanded symbolic action (“You, son of man, take one stick” (web:Ezek.37.16)). The row runs as one unbroken masoretic paragraph internally, framed only by the pe behind it at 37.14 and the samekh closing it at 37.28, so the tradition itself treats the demonstration (37.16-20) and its spoken interpretation (37.21-28, opened by a messenger formula with no addressee change) as a single section. Close: oshb:Ezek.37.28 carries a wide-family recognition close addressed to 'the nations' rather than the strict third-person plural (this expansion sits in the wider 64-verse recognition sweep, not the strict 28-verse list) -- וְיָֽדְעוּ֙ הַגּוֹיִ֔ם כִּ֚י אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה מְקַדֵּ֖שׁ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל בִּהְי֧וֹת מִקְדָּשִׁ֛י בְּתוֹכָ֖ם לְעוֹלָֽם -- with a samekh mark recorded immediately after. Both sides were weighed: the onset word-event at 37.15 is one of only 39 strict-form verses in the book, corroborated behind it by the pe at 37.14, and the samekh-marked recognition close at 37.28 is corroborated from the close side before the next word-event opens the following unit at oshb:Ezek.38.1.

boundary_rationale: Onset: the strict word-event formula opens the Gog complex at oshb:Ezek.38.1 וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (sweep: 39 verses strict form), immediately corroborated by the set-your-face direction opener at oshb:Ezek.38.2 בֶּן אָדָ֗ם שִׂ֤ים פָּנֶ֨יךָ֙ אֶל גּוֹג֙ אֶ֣רֶץ הַמָּג֔וֹג נְשִׂ֕יא רֹ֖אשׁ מֶ֣שֶׁךְ וְתֻבָ֑ל וְהִנָּבֵ֖א עָלָֽיו (sweep: 9 verses book-wide) and the messenger formula naming the addressee at oshb:Ezek.38.3. The unit runs as a paragraph chain rather than four separate rows: the messenger-formula reopenings at oshb:Ezek.38.10, oshb:Ezek.38.14 and oshb:Ezek.38.17 each change no addressee -- Gog stands as the referent throughout -- and none follows a refrain; the samekh marks recorded after oshb:Ezek.38.9, oshb:Ezek.38.13, oshb:Ezek.38.16 and oshb:Ezek.38.17 (four samekh, single-witness) therefore mark internal paragraphs rather than row seams, including a one-verse Masoretic paragraph at 38.17 itself. Two utterance-formula closes fall mid-unit at oshb:Ezek.38.18 and oshb:Ezek.38.21; both are paragraph-final rather than row-final because no fresh onset of the tracked classes follows either one, and the catastrophe description runs on without interruption. Close: the strict recognition formula closes the whole chapter at oshb:Ezek.38.23 וְהִתְגַּדִּלְתִּי֙ וְהִתְקַדִּשְׁתִּ֔י וְנ֣וֹדַעְתִּ֔י לְעֵינֵ֖י גּוֹיִ֣ם רַבִּ֑ים וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה (sweep: 28 verses strict form), with a samekh mark recorded immediately after -- a refrain-grade close corroborated by a masoretic mark, weighed against the son-of-man sub-onset that opens the following material at oshb:Ezek.39.1.

boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.39.1 opens וְאַתָּ֤ה בֶן אָדָם֙ הִנָּבֵ֣א עַל גּ֔וֹג וְאָ֣מַרְתָּ֔ כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה הִנְנִ֤י אֵלֶ֨יךָ֙ גּ֔וֹג נְשִׂ֕יא רֹ֖אשׁ מֶ֥שֶׁךְ וְתֻבָֽל, combining the ‘and you, son of man’ sub-onset with a messenger formula and the near-verbatim “Behold, I am against you, Gog” (web:Ezek.39.1, identically web:Ezek.38.3) verdict already given at oshb:Ezek.38.3. The row carries the temple/separate-place/building triad each measured at a hundred cubits (41:13-14), the rear building and its galleries with a K/Q lexical variant on 'galleries' at oshb:Ezek.41.15 (ואתוקיהא, checked: a form variant, not a numeral), the side-chamber gallery structure (41:16-19), the cherubim-and-palm-tree decorative program running to above the entrance (41:18-20), the doorposts of the nave (41:21), the wooden altar-table with its own speak-formula notice, וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלַ֔י זֶ֚ה הַשֻּׁלְחָ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֖ר לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.41.22), its speech rendered “This is the table that is before Yahweh” (web:Ezek.41.22), opened by the 'spoke to me' root, distinct from the 'said to me' form at 41:4, the double doors of the nave and sanctuary (41:23-25), and the repeated cherubim-and-palm-tree pattern closing on the porch threshold. Close side: 41:26 ends וְצַלְע֥וֹת הַבַּ֖יִת וְהָעֻבִּֽים (oshb:Ezek.41.26), “the side rooms of the temple and the thresholds” (web:Ezek.41.26), and the next verse, oshb:Ezek.42.1, moves the tour out to the outer court with its double transport verb, וַיּוֹצִאֵ֗נִי … וַיְבִאֵ֣נִי -- a strong close by contrast, since the following onset carries the counted double-transport device even though this row's own onset rests on the measured-object change rather than a formula. boundary_rationale: Onset side: 42:1 opens with a double transport verb, וַיּוֹצִאֵ֗נִי אֶל הֶֽחָצֵר֙ הַחִ֣יצוֹנָ֔ה ... וַיְבִאֵ֣נִי אֶל הַלִּשְׁכָּ֗ה (oshb:Ezek.42.1) “he brought me out into the outer court” (web:Ezek.42.1) ... “Then he brought me into the room” (web:Ezek.42.1) -- the strongest onset in the span after 40:1 and 43:1 -- moving the tour to the priests' chambers, first north-side (42:1-9) then, by parallel description, south-side (42:10-12). Close side: 42:13-14 supplies the row's function. The guide's naming speech closes the survey of these rooms by reading and not by formula: the וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י (oshb:Ezek.42.13) it carries is an onset-type device inside the vision, weighed below, and no close formula at all. These are the holy chambers where the priests “eat the most holy things” (web:Ezek.42.13) and must change garments before approaching the people -- a law-toned close inside a measurement row, disclosed rather than reclassified. The double transport at the onset is a licensed onset inside the vision, a stronger opening than a bare content shift would give; the close rests on the reading above rather than on a formula, and no parashah mark stands anywhere in these chapters to corroborate either edge (single-witness).

boundary_rationale: Onset side: 42:15 opens וְכִלָּ֗ה (oshb:Ezek.42.15) “when he had finished measuring the inner house” (web:Ezek.42.15) -- a completion notice, not a counted formula, pressed into onset service here, since it explicitly marks the end of the inner-house survey that has run since 40:5 before turning outward to the perimeter wall -- paired with the transport verb וְהוֹצִיאַ֨נִי֙ 'he brought me out', which makes 42:15 a verse of the counted guided-motion class (sweep: 33 verses / 46 occurrences) and gives the onset a licensed driver inside the vision. Four cardinal-direction measurements follow (east 42:16, north 42:17, south 42:18, west 42:19), each carrying its own measure verb, verse-initial at 42:16 and 42:17 and after the direction word at 42:18 and 42:19, then a summary at 42:20. Close side: 42:20 ends on the wall's purpose, לְהַבְדִּ֕יל בֵּ֥ין הַקֹּ֖דֶשׁ לְחֹֽל (oshb:Ezek.42.20) “to make a separation between that which was holy and that which was common” (web:Ezek.42.20) -- a genuine thematic close, and the point at which the whole measuring circuit that opened at 40:5 ends, immediately before 43:1's transport verb and the glory's return open a new kind of scene. Both sides of this seam are unusually well aligned: a completion-formula onset and a purpose-clause close on one side, a transport-plus-glory onset on the other.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: 43:1, a verse of the counted transport class (sweep: 33 verses / 46 occurrences), opens with וַיּוֹלִכֵ֖נִי אֶל הַשָּׁ֑עַר (oshb:Ezek.43.1) 'he led me to the gate', at the seam the book's division names as a hard seam, behind the closed measuring circuit, and the row immediately carries the glory-of-YHWH device twice (43:4, 43:5), part of the book's nine-verse departure/return arc for that idiom, alongside the river-Chebar inclusio at 43:3 (one of eight such verses tying this scene back to Ezek 1 and 10) and the prostration “and I fell on my face” (web:Ezek.43.3), one of five verses where the WEB reads “I fell on my face” (sweep: 5 verses). The row turns from vision report to direct address at 43:6-9: a voice from the house, the man beside the prophet, the 'son of man' charge naming YHWH's throne and footstool, and the polemic against the house of Israel's defilement of the sanctuary by royal corpses and high places. Close side: 43:9 ends the divine resolution וְשָׁכַנְתִּ֥י בְתוֹכָ֖ם לְעוֹלָֽם (oshb:Ezek.43.9) “Then I will dwell among them forever” (web:Ezek.43.9) immediately before the samekh (oshb:Ezek.43.9, single-witness) -- the first Masoretic paragraph mark since the pe at oshb:Ezek.39.29, ending a 103-verse unmarked stretch. This close is the first since the pe at 39:29 to carry a parashah mark, and it is disclosed as single-witness even so. Its near face carries no close-role formula: 43:9 ends on the divine resolution, which answers אֲשֶׁ֧ר אֶשְׁכָּן שָׁ֛ם בְּת֥וֹךְ בְּנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְעוֹלָ֑ם (oshb:Ezek.43.7) as an inclusio, and past the seam 43:10 opens 'you, son of man' to the same hearer after a verse that ends on no close-role formula, so the seam stands because the book's division names 43:1-9 as the vision and 43:10-12 as the torah of the house. A close of that kind holds this row at reduced confidence, though the onset's near face, the transport verse at 43:1, is licensed.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: 43:10 opens אַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֗ם (oshb:Ezek.43.10) 'you, son of man' directly after the samekh (single-witness) closing at oshb:Ezek.43.9 -- a near-form of the book's twenty-three-verse 'and you, son of man' sub-onset family, here without the leading vav, disclosed as such rather than counted against that sweep. It charges the prophet to show the house's pattern so Israel may be ashamed of its iniquities. Close side: 43:12 closes on a doubled envelope formula, זֹ֖את תּוֹרַ֣ת הַבָּ֑יִת ... הִנֵּה זֹ֖את תּוֹרַ֥ת הַבָּֽיִת (oshb:Ezek.43.12) “This is the law of the house” (web:Ezek.43.12) ... “Behold, this is the law of the house” (web:Ezek.43.12), repeating the title at the top and bottom of the same verse -- a strong lexical close-device, and the reason this three-verse span is held as its own row despite its length: the inclusio is a self-contained frame around 43:10-12 that a larger row would have to break through rather than around. The grade rests on these faces: the onset is a turn to the prophet without a counted device, since 43:10's address lacks the conjunction of the counted family, after a samekh on 43:9 that is no signal of its own; the close is the genre colophon in the composition's own voice, and its far face at 43:13 opens the altar's measurements with a list heading, which carries no signal on a far face; the stretch from the glory's return to the torah of the house is one whose division into units is held open, which keeps the row at reduced confidence and no lower.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: 43:13 opens with an explicit topic header, וְאֵ֨לֶּה מִדּ֤וֹת הַמִּזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ (oshb:Ezek.43.13), the vav-initial “These are the measurements of the altar” (web:Ezek.43.13), functioning as a list-onset in the same way such headers do elsewhere in the book, immediately after the doubled inclusio that closes 43:12. The row descends through the altar's base, lower and greater ledges, hearth and horns, in cubit-and-handbreadth units, one of which (43:15) carries two OSHB editors' notes, one marking an anomalous form and one recording a ketiv/qere decision the editors take with the Leningrad Codex against BHS, while the span's one K/Q note stands at 43:16. What the confidence this row carries rests on is that pairing at each seam: the altar list's own heading at 43:13 - a discourse turn carrying no formula - against the colophon that closes the torah of the house at 43:12 (oshb:Ezek.43.12), and a content close at 43:17 against the licensed speech at 43:18 (oshb:Ezek.43.18); the measuring survey does not extend to this span; and the division of this material is a held question, which caps the confidence at the level this row carries, no bespoke ground for less being stated here.

The utterance formula נְאֻ֛ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה (oshb:Ezek.43.19) stands inside 43:19, embedded between the relative clause about the priests near to me and the infinitive that follows it, so it closes nothing there, neither a paragraph nor the row, and the seven-day consecration instructions run on. The row carries the young-bull sin offering, the blood rite on the horns and corners, the second-day goat, the seven-day consecration, and closes at 43:27 on the same utterance formula, וְרָצִ֣אתִי אֶתְכֶ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.43.27) “Then I will accept you,’ says the Lord Yahweh” (web:Ezek.43.27), this time genuinely row-final. Close side: immediately after that utterance the verse carries two consecutive samekh marks, the sole doubled occurrence among the book's marked verses (sweep: 183 verses), single witness -- the close rests first on that verse-final utterance formula, with the doubled mark standing behind it as corroboration. Both sides converge unusually cleanly here: a messenger-formula onset opposite an utterance-plus-doubled-mark close.

Guided-motion verbs stand inside the measuring circuit, though not at its head: MEASURED over the pointed Hebrew witness, Ezek.47.3 does not BEGIN with a guided-motion verb (it opens בְּצֵאת הָאִ֥ישׁ) but does carry וַיַּעֲבִרֵ֥נִי later in the verse, and Ezek.47.4 carries that same form twice. The measuring sequence therefore remains texture inside the single river vision running 47.1-12, disclosed as a one-sentence category deviation rather than split into a separate row (oshb:Ezek.47.5, oshb:Ezek.47.3, oshb:Ezek.47.6).
